exposure: Previously scarred uterus (due to previous cesarean sections or D&C)
outcome: Fetal complications (low birth weight, preterm birth, low APGAR scores, NICU admissions)
cohort: A cohort of 1000 women, 500 with a history of vaginal delivery and 500 with a history of uterine scarring, were followed during a subsequent pregnancy.
finding: Uterine scarring (from previous C-sections or D&C) significantly increased the incidence of placenta previa in subsequent pregnancies, with a dose-dependent increase observed with more prior C-sections, and was associated with more cases of postpartum hemorrhage.
mod_finding: The study recommends encouraging vaginal birth as much as possible to reduce the risk of uterine scarring and subsequent placenta previa.
